newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares drop 0.6 pct on resistance.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares drop 0.6 pct on resistance.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted losses in afternoon selling on Wednesday after failing to overcome resistance at the index's 1,670-1,680 range for the third day in a row, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,649, down 10 points, or 0.6 percent from Tuesday. It brushed a high 1,681 in early trade before diving to 1,636 towards the close.
Trade volume jumped to 33.14 trillion lira from Tuesday's 28.18 trillion.
"The index retreated because it could not pierce the 1,670-1,680 band," said Mirsat Vardar from Info securities.

The index had soared four percent in the past two days, disregarding the possibility of early polls, after last week's 8.7 percent rally sparked by hopes of an alternative alliance to replace the troubled Islamist-conservative coalition.
Brokers said selective activity focused on shares of energy and state firms in an attempt to maintain market momentum on Wednesday and the market disregarded May inflation data announced early today.

"The concentration of turnover in energy and state firms was noticeable. I do not anticipate sharp falls because the chance of early elections has decreased. The index may drift sideways until the end of the week," said Melih Pastutmaz from Bayindir securities.

A small far-right party with a key position in parliament threatened on Wednesday to turn against Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan if he did not push through electoral reforms in their favour.

"If the electoral threshold is not brought down to five percent, we will bring down the coalition," Anatolian news agency quoted Orhan Kavuncu, vice chairman of the Grand Unity Party (BBP), as telling a news conference.

Erbakan announced on Sunday he would step down later this month to let True Path Party (DYP) leader and deputy Prime Minister head the government in the run-up to snap polls for which no date is yet proposed.
Under Turkish law parliament must set the polling date with a majority vote. The coalition has 274 seats in the 550-member parliament, with two seats vacant.

Analysts say even some government deputies may vote against early polls after only two years in office on fears they may not be reelected. The inability to pass an election law might give the secularist opposition the chance to set up a new coalition.

Of the 243 shares traded, falls outdid rises by 108 to 68 and 67 were stable. The IMKB Industrial eased 0.59 percent to 1,519, the IMKB Services jumped 2.55 percent to 1,648 and the IMKB Financial lost 1.73 percent to 1,813.
The index representing three power firms was the leading gainer with a 7.02 percent surge.

The most active shares were those of utilities Cukurova Elektrik, up 17,500 lira at 227,500, Aktas Elektrik, up 5,000 lira at 215,000 and largely state-owned petroleum products distributor Petrol Ofisi, up 500 lira at 25,500. They made up 41.1 percent of the total turnover.
